113: GEMARA: What is the [item given in exchange]? [If it is referring to] a coin - ["a coin" in the sense of] that which is usually given as money in exchange for something else, and the mishna is teaching us that although if it had been given under the rubric of money, which we have already established does not effect acquisition -- but if he gave it to him under the rubric of khalipin exchange it does effect acquisition.
One can learn from it, etc. - and we have established in Chapter "The Gold" that a coin cannot be used in a khalipin exchange. (Bava Metzia 46a:5)

Rav Yehuda said: this is what it is saying: With regard to all items that can be appraised when used as monetary value for another item - any item that, if one intended to use it as money to give in return for another item, it would be necessary to appraise its monetary value -- that is, any movable object other than a coin.
